about: Worked examples for the AI scorecard reader: real photos checked by a person digit by digit, with the right answer. Sent with every read so the AI learns how these scorebooks are filled in. README: How the AI reader learns -> Worked examples.

lessons: Read HOW OUT, BOWLER and the score on the SAME row as the batter - never shift them to the next batter.
A circled number in the BOWLER column is a shirt number: find it beside a name in the bowling list.
In the bowling boxes a circled corner number is the bowler's running runs; LB / BOW / CT / ST are wickets; plain W is a wide.
Overs = boxes used. Use null for numbers you can't work out.
Runs come from the TOTAL column at the right of each row, not the scribbles and not the batting-order numbers on the left.
The grand total is the last number in the over-by-over score column when there is no G. TOTAL.
A bowler can be written above the BOWLER heading ('9. TONY') - include him.
